archetype.name: Lost Season (worse record than its play)
archetype.definition: A last-place, 100-loss year built on the league's weakest lineup, made a few games uglier than it deserved by a near-league-worst showing in close games.

report.headline: A better team than 2025 that lost ten more games anyway

recap.finish: 62-100; last in the AL West, 19 games behind HOU, missed the postseason
recap.body:
The Angels finished 30th of 30 on the site, and the root cause is not hard to find. The lineup posted the league's worst OPS (.679) and ranked 29th in runs per game, and the hitters graded an F. The run prevention was only middling: a 4.29 team ERA ranked 21st, run prevention ranked 22nd, and the fielders cost 22.5 runs. A club that scored about 4.0 runs a game and allowed about 4.6 was never going to contend, and it didn't.

The record overstates how bad the play was, though. They were outscored 752 to 655, a run differential of -0.6 per game that typically produces around 70 wins, not 62. The W vs Run Diff of -8.8 ranked 29th, and the monthly lines show it. August was an 11-17 month in which they outscored opponents 99-97. June was 13-14 with a positive margin. Last season was the mirror image: 2025's 72-90 came with a -1.01 run differential and a +7.0 W vs Run Diff. By the margin, this team was clearly better than last year's. By the standings, it was ten games worse.

The arc was a slow sink rather than a collapse. After a 3-3 opening week they went 9-17 in April and 11-17 in May, when the staff allowed 145 runs, its worst month. June was the one stretch of competent baseball. July then broke the season: 6-17 while scoring just 75 runs in 23 games, about 3.3 a night. August and September added 20 more losses. The longest losing streak was only seven games, but the longest winning streak was only four, so there was never a run to build on. They closed 4-6, dropping the last two in Seattle, and finished two games behind the Athletics for fourth.

What worked was concentrated in a few players. Reid Detmers was a legitimate front-line starter: 4.9 WAR, a 3.36 ERA backed by a 3.01 FIP, and 211 strikeouts in 185 innings. Walbert Ureña added 2.6 WAR and a 2.97 ERA over 148 innings, though his 3.62 FIP and 10.9% walk rate say some of that was fortune. Zach Neto (3.9 WAR, 27 HR, 24 SB, 116 wRC+) and the All-Star Mike Trout (129 wRC+, .382 OBP) anchored the lineup, and Wade Meckler (120 wRC+) and Nolan Schanuel (111) were productive part-timers. The rotation still graded C- because the back three were poor: Ryan Johnson, Grayson Rodriguez and Yusei Kikuchi combined for 1.4 WAR across roughly 266 innings, and Rodriguez's ERA was 6.02.

The lineup's holes were everywhere outside that core. Oswald Peraza (74 wRC+), Moisés Ballesteros (72), Josh Lowe (76) and Jorge Soler (87, -0.6 WAR) took more than 1,400 plate appearances between them at below-replacement or near-replacement quality. The bullpen graded C- with no real anchor among its innings leaders. Samy Natera Jr. was the exception, striking out 36.6% of batters with a 1.90 FIP, but he threw only 31.2 innings.

highlights.title: Detmers pitched like an ace
highlights.body: Detmers ranked 13th of 215 starters, and his peripherals were better than his already strong ERA. A 28.5% strikeout rate against a 6.5% walk rate is the profile of a repeatable top-of-rotation arm, not a lucky season. He is the one unambiguous building block on the staff.

highlights.title: Underlying margin improved from 2025
highlights.body: The run differential per game improved from -1.01 to -0.6. Run prevention also climbed from 28th to 22nd, and the fielding hole shrank from -52.1 runs to -22.5. None of that shows in the record, but it means this roster played closer to a 70-win level than the standings suggest.

highlights.title: Neto and Trout carried the lineup
highlights.body: Neto's 3.9 WAR across 704 plate appearances, with power and speed, made him the club's best position player. Trout's .382 OBP and 129 wRC+ made him the best bat. Together they were most of what the offense had.

lowlights.title: League-worst offense, again
lowlights.body: The .679 OPS ranked dead last. Four regulars sat well below average by wRC+, and the catcher, second-base and DH spots produced almost nothing. This isn't new: the offense ranked 28th, 25th and now 29th in runs over three seasons, so it is a structural problem rather than a slump.

lowlights.title: Close games went badly wrong
lowlights.body: Winning about nine fewer games than the run differential implies ranked 29th in the league. August is the clearest example: the club outscored opponents and still went 11-17. Records like that mostly even out, as the swing from +7.0 in 2025 shows.

lowlights.title: July sank the season
lowlights.body: A 6-17 month with only 75 runs scored ended any pretense of respectability. It followed the team's best stretch in June. The offense, not the pitching, was the culprit: 105 runs allowed was roughly the season's per-game norm.

arc.note: Poor April and May, a near-.500 June with a positive margin, then a 6-17 July that buried the year. The final two months were played out at a loser's pace despite an even run differential in August.

recap.nextYear: The numbers say this was roughly a 70-win roster that got 62. Some of the -8.8 W vs Run Diff should come back on its own, the way 2025's +7.0 didn't hold. The foundation is narrow but real. Detmers is a top-15 starter by the site's rankings. Neto and Trout carried the lineup, and Meckler and Schanuel hit well in part-time roles. Ureña's ERA likely runs closer to his 3.62 FIP. The work list is long: the hitters graded F with catcher, second base and DH as black holes. The back of the rotation gave about 266 innings of below-average work. The bullpen's C- had only Natera's small-sample dominance to recommend it. The fielding improved but still ranked 25th. Better luck alone might lift this team to the low 70s. Getting further than that requires the offense to stop finishing at the bottom of the league.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; the run differential and the close-game luck reading are both clear-cut.
